title: Overlays stay off what learners need
statement: Never let a caption, control, card, panel border or crop cover or cut what the learner still needs, such as teaching text, a clue or a character's face.
example: A feedback popup covered three clues the learner needed for the next answer.
detail: Native captures found a film's default caption covering the slide text, a centred Play button covering instructional diagrams on several films, and a fixed feedback popup over three glowing clues needed for the next answer (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json`, lines 2451 and 2419). A supplied UI review of another lesson found the play button over the speaking character's face, over the figures a mid-video check asks about and over one of the things the screen teaches (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/aladdin-p1-ui-review.reference.md`, line 42). The repairs gave captions and labelled controls reserved space outside the picture, moved film controls to a strip beneath the video, and kept clue feedback off the passage (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/NAVIGATION-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW-by-residual.md`, line 18).

evidence.quote: Default caption covers the slide text Topics name a subject; central blue Play covers instructional diagrams on several other G5 films.
Captions and labelled playback controls occupy reserved space outside the picture.
Actual: fixed feedback popup overlays three glowing clues needed for the next answer.
Expected: feedback readable below clue box/right panel/margin and never covering active passage.

Centre placement puts it over the speaking character's face, over the running figures the learner is being asked about in the mid-video check, and over "BUT something changes", one of the five things the story-grammar screen teaches.
Peter Pan film controls occupy a permanent strip beneath the contained video, retaining the native video's object-fit/ratio behaviour.
Expected: preserve the principal character’s face when adapting portrait artwork to the tablet banner.
On L4/p27 the natural artwork is 848×1264, rendered in a 753×410 box.
`film.tsx:321` uses a fill image; the surrounding `.bk-art img` rule uses `object-fit: cover`, which crops instructional poster text.
Moving these slides into the ordinary full-bleed art slot would crop labels and source notes. Text-heavy posters should not acquire a title/button overlay over their instructional words.
A comic-panel gutter previously crossed Cassio’s face. That defect was corrected in the later visual treatment. Treat it as a concrete composition regression test.
Recheck image continuity and the Cassio composition.
